# With several merged folders at one name key, exactly one takes over the live folder made again (filesystem §5.10). The sim's ignore_rules covers the byte-equal pick in both creation orders, the lowest-ID pick in both orders, the pick that differs from the live name only in Unicode normalization (taken over without a rename, in both orders), and the folder left behind uploading once moved away or going once deleted; the engine's ignore tests cover three folders (byte-equal, case-only lowest ID, normalization-equal over a lower ID, and two normalization-equal folders decided by ID). Mutants of the byte-equal preference, the normalization tier, the ID order, the pick, the planner exemption for the folders left behind, and the oracle's normalization-aware name check each fail at least one of them, and none of the earlier tests has two merged folders at one key.
# The planner lets only the node that holds the live ID rename past the merged folders at its key. A sim test runs a live folder made again with its effects planned before and after the commit build that settles the merged folders, for one folder and for two, and an engine test checks that no folder is created beside merged folders at the key before one takes the live folder over, which holds on any disk. A mutant that lets the exemption cover every remote folder fails both, and no earlier test plans effects before that commit build. An engine test pins that the node holding the live ID still waits behind a merged folder when it moves into the key from another folder; a mutant that exempts any node with a local copy fails only it.
# One ignored sim test records GUN-1431: a file made at the name after a freed merge folder's create is built still gets that folder conflict-renamed and its left-out file published.
# The model change settles a merged folder against whichever live folder holds its name key now. Each branch of that rule has its own scenario test in the sim's ignore_rules, and a mutant of each branch fails only that branch's tests: a new local folder when no live folder holds the key (delete here, delete elsewhere, rename elsewhere, move elsewhere), a takeover of a live folder this device never synced (one made at the name, and two devices freeing the same folder), waiting while this device's own delete is in flight, a new folder when the user moved the live folder into the merged one, waiting for a merged parent (nested merge), waiting while a live file holds the key, named in the problem (with a pattern rule and with an anchored rule), waiting while this device keeps another folder at the key (a kept folder takes the new live folder over), and keeping a synced entry added offline in the merged folder.
# Six of these come from review probes that fail on the previous head, and no earlier test reaches those states. The earlier tests cover the merged folder only while the folder it merged into stays live at the key.
# The driver test runs the free-key path on a real case-sensitive volume, because the sim does not model the driver's checkpoint after a free.
# The engine_sync harness excuses a merged folder whose problem names the live server entry at its name key, which is how the folder is reported while that entry holds the key. A battery case (cc-e8c3e483) is checked in for that state, and a unit test of the harness predicate fails when it accepts a live node that does not hold the key.
# The review of 5be054ab added seven tests, each red on that head or under a named mutant: a file at the name key holds the merged folder (red under a folder-only takeover filter); the merged folder uploads under a new ID after the move when the user moved the live folder away here, in the engine and in the sim (red when that branch waits), and after the delete when the user deleted it here (red when the takeover accepts a holder this device synced); an ignored parked node goes back to its free place while a merged folder holds its server name, and every folder of a chain of moves onto a merged folder, of length 2, 3 and 5, stays unparked and is reported behind it (each red on 5be054ab and under a mutant of its own fix; the chain test also fails when parkable checks only a direct hold); the harness predicate rejects a stale alias target outside a merged parent (red when it accepts any alias target).
# The review of 3ef45feb added seven tests, all on one shared setup helper. In the engine: a park planned before its folder falls behind a merged folder through a chain is refused while the chain stands and allowed once it goes; a swap beside such a chain still resolves; a chain through an excluded folder is reported as held by that folder; a parked node the rules leave out is not unparked onto a merged folder; and a source check fails when any function other than the destination checks asks the direct question, naming keeps_in_place as the fix. In the sim: a park queued before its folder falls behind a merged folder leaves the folder in place and the folder syncs once the chain goes, and a park planned during a swap does not apply once the chain reaches a merged folder. The chain test now runs lengths 2, 3, 5 and 20. Each test fails on 3ef45feb or under a mutant of the line it protects: permits checking only a direct hold, the way_out residue check removed, or the stop at an excluded holder removed.
# The review of b6ea32f1 added three tests for which holder the planner sees at a name key that several nodes share. A swap of two folders while a merged folder holds one of their keys parks neither folder, in the engine and in the sim, where both stay in place, are reported behind the merged folder, and the quiet oracle names the live-entry hold. A parked file whose server place is held by both an excluded folder and a merged folder goes home, and a file moving there is reported held by the excluded folder. The swap tests fail without the rank or with excluded-first only; the go-home test fails with merged-first only.
# The review of 5debd583 added one sim test: a parked file whose server name is exactly a merged folder, beside an excluded folder at the same key, goes back to its free home. It fails on every earlier head and when the merged-folder check runs on the server place before the planner picks where the node goes. The go-home engine test gained a case where the merged folder is excluded too, so the file still goes home and a file moving there is reported behind the merged folder.
# Commit H added six sim tests for a merged folder that takes over a live folder whose local copy sits below it, after another device moved that folder out: the base case, a file made in the nested copy before the takeover, a file written there between planning the removal and applying it, a left-out file in the nested copy, a file at the name of an entry moving up, and a crash at every step. All six fail on the previous head; a sim disk that removes a non-empty folder fails the write-before-apply and left-out tests, and a takeover that leaves the nested entries their old synced parent or gives the nested copy no synced shape fails all six.
